obligations.expected: The clk period is 10 ns; rst_b is active-low and asynchronously resets control and arithmetic register state. All inputs are driven on falling edges, and outputs are sampled after they stabilize following rising edges. valid is zero during reset; when valid=0, no numerical guarantee is made for the floating-point data, including old outputs during reset.

obligations.stimulus: Construct within-frame changes, successive distinct captures, and changes near capture boundaries, covering previous/current image history and boundary mixing for channel 31 at the final position; include zero, positive/negative, and distinguishable spatial images. Actual pixel changes must cover the target history.
obligations.expected:
Starting from reset deassertion, count rising edges with en=1; non-enabled edges do not increment this count. On every 288th enabled edge, atomically capture mem at that edge; changes in mem at all other times do not affect image storage, and mem is allowed to change every cycle. Reset clears the previously captured image to all zeros. Continuous operation has no per-frame ready or acceptance signal.

Each capture edge produces one eventual result to be output, using the previously captured image A and the current image B. The main mathematics is the computation of the network below on A, with an exception for depthwise convolution input channel 31 corresponding to pooling position 8: its convolution patches for depthwise convolution rows 16 and 17 are computed from B. All other depthwise convolution rows/channels come from A; in particular, position 7 still uses A, and position 7 must not be changed as a side effect of first replacing the last four rows of the complete convolution tensor. A for the first capture is the reset zero image. This boundary mixing is part of the definition of this problem and naturally reduces to the complete mathematical network when the same image is maintained; transition outputs must not be ignored.

obligations.stimulus: Using legal signed8 images that distinguish convolution, fixed-point truncation, and activation, predict the 32 11×7 kernels and their public outputs through an independent mathematical model; cover signs and nonuniform spatial patterns.
obligations.expected: Conv_Weight is ordered by output channel, kernel row, and kernel column, 32×11×7; Conv_Bias has one entry per channel. The image has no padding and a stride of one, producing 20×4 values per channel: the bias plus the sum of the corresponding 11×7 signed products. Fixed-point activation is defined as first multiplying the sum by the given multiplier and truncating to signed 32 bits, then arithmetically right-shifting by the given number of bits, and finally clamping to 0–127; there is no rounding. The first-layer multiplier is 111 and the shift is 14. All accumulations and multiplications retain the low 32 bits; pixels and weights are interpreted as eight-bit two's complement, and biases as signed 32-bit values. Integers in the parameter files are the corresponding signed values.

obligations.description: Depthwise convolution, pointwise convolution, and pooling
obligations.setup: Establish the legal history required for this obligation through the native public interface, satisfying public initialization and deterministic valid windows, without accessing hidden state.
obligations.stimulus: Use legal images that distinguish spatial/channel indexing and maximum selection to check DW3×3, PW channel accumulation, 2×2 pooling, and flattening order; cover relevant history across capture boundaries.
obligations.expected:
The order of DWConv_Weight is input channel, then 3×3 kernel row/column, with one DWConv_Bias entry per channel. For each channel, apply unpadded 3×3 convolution with stride one to the first-layer 20×4, obtaining 18×2; the activation multiplier is 59 and the shift is 11. Only the channels/rows specified by R-MCNN-002 use B's first-layer convolution patches.

The order of PWConv_Weight is output channel, then input channel, 32×32; PWConv_Bias has one entry per output channel. At each spatial point, sum the products over 32 input channels and add the bias, with activation multiplier 69 and shift 13, producing 32×18×2. For each channel, non-overlapping 2×2 max pooling forms nine values; positions p=0–8 use rows 2p and 2p+1 and two columns. All pooled values are nonnegative eight-bit values, with flattened index channel×9+p. A position-major weight flattening order must not be used.

obligations.stimulus: Use multiple distinguishable images to produce changes in the fully connected layer and LUT indices, and check accumulation of 288 terms, bias, multiplication by 11, arithmetic shift by 15, the low eight-bit index, and the two classes of 32-bit outputs; predictions must not be derived from actual.
obligations.expected: Linear_Weight is ordered by output class and flattened index, 2×288; Linear_Bias has one entry per class. Each class logit is the bias plus the sum of products of 288 pooled values and their corresponding signed weights, retaining signed 32 bits. Multiply the logit by 11, truncate to 32 bits, arithmetically right-shift by 15, and then retain only the low eight bits as the LUT address. These eight bits use truncation wraparound, with no additional saturation: for example, even if the arithmetic right-shift result is outside −128 to 127, the low eight bits are still taken. The 256 entries in sigmoid_lookup_table.txt are arranged by unsigned eight-bit address, with positive-value addresses first and negative-value addresses following in two's-complement bit-pattern order; float_out0/1 must match the corresponding 32-bit hexadecimal data bit for bit.
